source.title: LLM Unlearning on Noisy Forget Sets: A Study of Incomplete, Rewritten, and Watermarked Data
source.authors: Chang-Sheng Wang; Yihua Zhang; Dennis Wei; Jing-Han Jia; Pin-Yu Chen; Si-Jia Liu

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how perturbing the training forget set affects unlearning, not whether post-unlearning attacks recover knowledge or whether unlearning deletes it from weights. Recovery attacks appear only in related-work discussion and citations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own unlearning efficacy and utility results under noisy forget-set training; these are recorded as findings not covered by versions A–F. Mentions of post-unlearning fine-tuning and jailbreak attacks in related work are not experimental results from this study. Hyperparameter-search values and illustrative generations are not recorded as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study varies the training-time forget set (masking, rewriting, watermarking) for RMU and NPO and reports unlearning efficacy and utility. It runs no post-unlearning recovery attack: no relearning, ablation, quantization or prompting. It never asks whether knowledge is deleted or only blocked. Attacks (jailbreaks, relearning) appear only in related work. Its clean-data RMU result (WMDP 0.32 vs 0.64, MMLU 0.569 vs 0.581) restates WMDP's own setting. Without any attack it cannot bear on version A's robustness clause, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that RMU and NPO are robust to masked, rewritten and watermarked forget data when core semantic cues are kept, explained by preserved salient tokens. Heavy masking (>30%) and strong watermarks degrade efficacy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RMU and NPO unlearning, but changes the training forget-set format to masking, rewriting, and watermarking; it does not evaluate post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Unlearning outcomes vary with mask ratio and watermark strength: the authors report degradation beyond about 30% masking and at stronger KGW/SynthID settings.

fits_no_version.finding: RMU and NPO keep similar efficacy and utility when the forget set is 30% masked, rewritten, or lightly watermarked. Efficacy degrades above about 30% masking and at KGW δ≥4 or SynthID m=6. Error sets overlap above 93% with clean-data unlearning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time unlearning efficacy is robust to moderate semantic-preserving perturbation of the forget set but degrades under strong masking or watermarking.

fits_no_version.finding: Utility (MMLU or MUSE retain KnowMem) stays near clean-data values for most perturbations; NPO on WMDP loses substantial MMLU even on clean data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy forget-set training has modest, condition-dependent utility effects.

record.peer_reviewed: AISec ’25 (Proceedings of the 2025 Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security)
record.problems: The study does not test any of the listed post-unlearning recovery attacks or directly distinguish removal from blocked access. Evidence covers two benchmarks and two methods, with the WMDP experiments centered on Zephyr-7B-beta and MUSE-Books on ICLM-7B. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Some masking and saliency results are figure-only, and exact point values are not available in the text for the masking-ratio sweep.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 2's Original Model comparator rows and the RMU Original Data rows duplicated in Table 3. Also omitted exact per-ratio Figure 2 values (figure-only), Figure 3 error-set overlap values, Figure 4 salient-token comparisons, and Table 5 illustrative examples; these concern consistency or token saliency rather than post-unlearning recovery.

untested.parts: Whether any simple attack recovers the unlearned knowledge; only post-unlearning efficacy and utility without attacks are reported.
No activation ablation or deletion-vs-blocking analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context probes.
No new robust method claimed or tested against attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Internal inconsistency in the source: Sec. 5.1.1 says only RMU is run on WMDP, yet Table 2 and Fig. 1/2 report NPO on WMDP. The study's own scope never touches recovery or shallowness. The relation could arguably be uses_without_test/T4, since it relies on RMU and NPO as working tools, but no verdict changes either way.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether simple post-unlearning attacks recover targeted knowledge; its results concern training with perturbed forget data.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access blocking versus deletion is tested.
No prompt-rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
No newer counter-method is tested for resistance to the listed recovery attacks.
